q.t: What is the digit sum of 345?
q.e: Add the digits: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.

q.t: Which of these is a palindrome?
q.e: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards: 8-4-8.

q.t: In a row of numbers, a supercell is a cell whose number is …
o: the largest in the whole table
q.e: It only has to beat the cells right next to it, not the whole table.

q.t: How many 2-digit numbers are there (10 to 99)?
q.e: From 10 to 99 inclusive: 99 − 10 + 1 = 90.

q.t: How many 1-digit numbers are there (1 to 9)?
Collatz rule: what comes after 12?
q.e: 12 is even, so halve it: 6.

q.t: Collatz rule: what comes after 5?
q.e: 5 is odd, so multiply by 3 and add 1: 16.

q.t: Kaprekar's constant for 4-digit numbers is …
q.e: Repeating 'largest arrangement − smallest arrangement' always lands on 6174.

q.t: A child at the END of a line can never say …
q.e: An end child has only one neighbour, so at most one person next to them can be taller.

q.t: Reverse and add: 12 + 21 = ?
q.e: 33 reads the same both ways — a palindrome in one step.

q.t: What is the smallest number whose digit sum is 14?
q.e: Use as few digits as possible (two, since one digit maxes at 9). The last digit can be at most 9, so the first is at least 14 − 9 = 5: 59.

q.t: What is the largest 5-digit number whose digit sum is 14?
q.e: Make the leftmost digits as big as possible: 9, then 14 − 9 = 5, then zeros → 95000.

q.t: How many times does the digit 7 appear when you write 1 to 100?
q.e: 10 times in the units place (7, 17, …, 97) and 10 in the tens place (70–79). 77 counts twice.

q.t: How many 3-digit numbers are there?
Kaprekar step from 6382: largest − smallest arrangement = ?
Can a 4-digit number + a 2-digit number ever give a 6-digit number?
q.e: Test the extreme: even the biggest possible sum has only 5 digits.

q.t: 5-digit number + 5-digit number gives a 5-digit number. This is …
Five children of different heights say how many neighbours are taller. Is 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 possible?
o: No — the tallest child must say 0
q.e: Nobody is taller than the tallest child, so that child always says 0.

q.t: In 21 (add 1, 2 or 3; first to 21 wins), which number should you say just before your last move?
q.e: From 17 the opponent can only reach 18, 19 or 20, and from each of those you can reach 21.

q.t: A grid has 8 columns and 4 rows, every cell 32. What is the total?
q.e: There are 8 × 4 = 32 cells of 32, so 32 × 32 = 1024 — multiply instead of adding one by one.

q.t: How many times does the digit 7 appear when you write 1 to 1000?
q.e: 100 times each in the units, tens and hundreds places: 300.

q.t: What is the sum of the smallest and largest 5-digit palindromes?
What is the difference between the largest and smallest 5-digit palindromes?
3-digit Kaprekar: which number do the steps settle on?
The clock shows 10:01. How many minutes until the next palindromic time?
q.e: The next one is 11:11, which is 1 hour 10 minutes = 70 minutes later.

q.t: In a row of 9 cells with no repeated numbers, what is the MOST supercells possible?
q.e: Two supercells can't be neighbours, so at best they alternate: cells 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

q.t: Can a table with no repeated numbers have NO supercells?
o: No — the cell with the largest number is always one
q.e: Nothing is bigger than the largest number, so it beats all its neighbours.

q.t: Reverse and add starting from 68: 68 + 86 = 154, 154 + 451 = 605, 605 + 506 = ?
q.e: 605 + 506 = 1111, a palindrome.

q.t: Collatz sequence from 21: 21 → 64 → … How many steps until you reach 1?
Can 5-digit − 5-digit equal 91,500?
q.e: Both numbers must have 5 digits, so the biggest gap is 89,999.

q.t: I am a 5-digit odd palindrome. My tens digit is double my units digit, and my hundreds digit is double my tens digit. Who am I?
q.e: Units is odd and doubling twice must stay a single digit, so units = 1, tens = 2, hundreds = 4. Mirror it: 12421.

q.t: How many rounds does 6382 take to reach 6174 by Kaprekar's method?
In the game of 21 (add 1–3), which numbers should the winning player say?
q.e: Each pair of turns can be made to add exactly 4 (opponent adds x, you add 4 − x), so the winning numbers are 4 apart, ending at 21.

q.t: Game: add 1 to 10 each turn, first to reach 99 wins. Which player can always win?
q.e: Pairs of turns can be made to total 11, and 99 = 9 × 11. The first player can't reach 11 on the first move, so the second player takes every multiple of 11.

q.t: Start at 0, add 1–3 each turn, first to 22 wins. What should the first player say first?
q.e: Winning numbers go down in 4s from 22: 18, 14, 10, 6, 2. Say 2 and keep landing on them.

q.t: Sheetal (Grade 6) says she has spent 13,000 hours in school. About how many years is that at 6 hours a day, 200 days a year?
o: About 11 years — too many for a Grade 6 student
q.e: 6 × 200 = 1,200 hours a year. 13,000 ÷ 1,200 ≈ 11 years, but she's been in school only about 7–8 years.

q.t: Which consecutive-digit 3-digit number has digit sum 21?
q.e: The digit sum of three consecutive digits is 3 × the middle digit. 21 = 3 × 7, so the middle digit is 7: 678.

q.t: Using any number of 1500s and 400s, which of these CANNOT be made?
Collatz from 100 passes through which odd number first?
q.e: 100 → 50 → 25. 25 is the first odd number reached.

q.t: How many 3-digit palindromes are there in all (101 to 999)?
q.k: len([i for i in range(100,1000) if str(i)==str(i)[::-1]])
q.e: First digit (= last digit) 1–9: 9 choices; middle digit 0–9: 10 choices. 9 × 10 = 90.
